binary systems are crucial for interpreting gravitational wave data.  In these calculations, the dynamics of the system are typically divided into three distinct phases: inspiral, merger, and ringdown.  The phase of the inspiral is characterized by the gradual decrease in the orbital period, which is accompanied by the emission of gravitational waves.  In this paper, we have developed a new approach to modeling the phase of the inspiral, which is based on the assumption that the dynamics of the system can be described by a set of equations that are valid for all values of the orbital separation.  This approach is in contrast to the traditional method of modeling the phase of the inspiral, which relies on the assumption that the dynamics of the system can be described by a set of equations that are valid only for large values of the orbital separation.  Our new approach has been shown to be in good agreement with the results of numerical simulations for a wide range of binary systems, including those consisting of black holes and neutron stars.
